title: PD-1 Inhibitors vs Docetaxel in 2nd-line Advanced NSCLC
background: Second-line treatment for advanced NSCLC after first-line chemo-immunotherapy remains uncertain. Recent trials (e.g. KEYNOTE-010, CheckMate 017, ORIENT-3, RATIONALE-303) individually show PFS/OS benefit vs docetaxel, but no updated aggregate since the 2024 meta (18 trials). A decision-relevant question: do PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors as a class improve OS in 2nd-line, and does PD-L1 TPS modify the effect? (Dedup layer 3: 4 meta-analyses 2021-2026 identified.)

pico.P: Non-small cell lung cancer, stage IV, 2nd-line (after 1st-line platinum-based ± IO)
pico.I: PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors (nivolumab, pembrolizumab, atezolizumab, durvalumab, sintilimab, tislelizumab, toripalimab, camrelizumab)

search_terms.P: carcinoma, non-small-cell lung[Mesh] AND (second-line OR previously treated)
search_terms.I: nivolumab OR pembrolizumab OR atezolizumab OR durvalumab OR sintilimab OR tislelizumab OR toripalimab OR camrelizumab

meta_type_rationale: Two-arm RCTs (PD-1 vs docetaxel); pairwise with random-effects DL model, subgroup by PD-L1 TPS. Not NMA (no ≥3 simultaneous arms in a connected network); IPD not required (published summary HRs sufficient).

score_anchors.clinical: OS/PFS benefit is a real clinical decision for 2nd-line therapy selection; magnitude still debated by class vs single drug
score_anchors.feasibility: Clean 2-arm design, standard effect measures (HR for time-to-event, RR for ORR); no missing-data reconstruction needed
score_anchors.data: Published summary HRs available for ~10 RCTs; 2 trials require hazard-ratio extraction from KM (moderate effort)
score_anchors.novelty: 2024 meta covered 18 trials but without PD-L1 TPS subgroup; 3 post-2024 trials add evidence (verified in dedup layer 3)
